data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a small gross reserve release of GBP 0.557 million for the 2015 and prior underwriting years, as calculated from the claims development triangle. This release contributed to the 2015 year of account closing with a profit, a significant improvement from its initial forecast loss. The report generally highlights a trend of improving underlying loss ratios, but also details significant adverse development from large losses and natural catastrophes, particularly Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria (HIMM) in 2016 and 2017, which impacted various lines of business.
raw_causal_phrases: promising trend of improvement in the syndicate's underlying loss ratios
Falling oil prices led to a fall in premium income written in Lloyd's

The hull account ran at a net loss ratio of 149% and sustained a net underwriting loss of GBP 7m. These losses were caused by a combination of a large loss of GBP 1.6m and a higher than expected incidence of attritional claims.

The property account ran at a net loss ratio of 117% and sustained a net underwriting loss of GBP 0.5m. Contributing to this loss were two catastrophe losses which impacted the portfolio disproportionately.
The cargo, energy, liability and non-marine property accounts all ran profitably

The property account is running at a net loss ratio of 105% and was impacted by HIMM.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development calculated from gross claims development triangle for 2015 underwriting year only, as 2016 and 2017 are considered current/recent years. The narrative focuses on adverse development for recent underwriting years, but the calculated PYD for 2015 and prior is a release, consistent with the 2015 YOA moving from a large initial loss to a small profit at closure.
